core_obligations: Let a diagram of the valuative criterion be given with two morphisms a, b : Spec(A) -> X fitting into it (proof lines 9192-9195).
Identify the equalizer Z of a and b with the fibre product Spec(A) x_{(a,b), X x_Y X, Delta} X (proof lines 9196-9197).
Use separatedness of f to see that Z is a closed subscheme of Spec(A) containing the generic point (proof lines 9198-9200).
Conclude Z = Spec(A) because A is a domain, hence a = b, which is the uniqueness part (proof lines 9200-9201).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if f : X -> Y is a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over S, then f satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion (source lines 9184-9190). The proof is an equalizer argument: given a diagram and two morphisms a, b : Spec(A) -> X fitting into it, the equalizer Z of a and b is the fibre product Spec(A) x_{(a,b), X x_Y X, Delta} X; since f is separated the diagonal is a closed immersion, so Z is a closed subscheme of Spec(A) containing the generic point, and because A is a domain this forces Z = Spec(A), hence a = b.
